outcome: Length of first stage of labor
cohort: 738 women in labor from a tertiary hospital in New Zealand
finding: Fetal malposition (OP/OT) compared to occiput-anterior (OA) position was associated with increased oxytocin augmentation, epidural use, longer first stage of labor, fewer normal vaginal births, and more cesarean sections, but not with adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Fetal malposition (OP/OT) was associated with fewer normal vaginal births and more cesarean sections.
